title: Withdrawal of a Pending Enrollment — Commercial Natural Gas Supply Terms
content:
**1. No rescission period.** Commercial Natural Gas Supply enrollments carry no statutory rescission period.

**2. Withdrawal before confirmation.** A business may withdraw a pending enrollment only while the gas utility has not yet confirmed it, that is while the utility confirmation date on the agreement is empty, and only when the plan permits withdrawal before confirmation.

**3. After confirmation.** Once the utility has confirmed the enrollment, the business can end the agreement only by cancelling after supply starts, and the early termination fee rules apply.

**4. Evidence.** Whether the utility has confirmed is read from the utility confirmation date on the record of the agreement being withdrawn. A withdrawn enrollment moves from enrollment pending to withdrawn.

## Clause 2 as a table

| Utility confirmation date on the agreement | Plan permits withdrawal before confirmation | May the business withdraw? |
|---|---|---|
| Empty | Yes | Yes |
| Empty | No | No |
| Recorded | Yes | No; the agreement can be ended only by cancelling after supply starts |
| Recorded | No | No; the agreement can be ended only by cancelling after supply starts |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A café enrolled its site on a Beacon Ridge Commercial Gas plan last week; the agreement is enrollment pending and the utility confirmation date is empty. The café may withdraw the enrollment.
- A print shop's enrollment shows a utility confirmation date, though supply has not yet started. The shop can no longer withdraw; it can end the agreement only by cancelling after supply starts, and the early termination fee rules then apply.
